1.5 Initial categories and coproducts

Mapping animae allow us to express universal properties for functors out of a category. We use them to introduce the initial category and coproducts.

Axiom B.4 (Initial category). There is a category \(\emptyset \), called the initial category, such that \(\Map (\emptyset ,T)\) is contractible for every category \(T\).

Thus there is a functor \(\emptyset \to T\) for every \(T\), and for any two such functors their anima of identifications is contractible. Indeed, their representing points lie in the contractible anima \(\Map (\emptyset ,T)\), and Lemma 1.3.10 and Construction 1.4.1 give the assertion about animae of identifications.

Agda The functor from the initial category

Agda Transporting contractibility through representing points

contractible-iso

Derivation, checked

contractible-iso : {C X : CAT} → IsContractible C
  → (f g : MAP X C) → IsContractible (f ＝ g)
Proof / implementation
contractible-iso {C} e f g = contractible-source (postWhisker (terminate C))
  (postWhisker-isEquiv (terminate C) e f g)
  (terminalIso-isEquiv (terminate C ∘ f) (terminate C ∘ g))

contractible-source

Derivation, checked

contractible-source : {C D : CAT} (f : MAP C D)
  → IsEquiv f → IsContractible D → IsContractible C
Proof / implementation
contractible-source {C} {D} f e h = equiv-transport
  (terminal-iso (terminate D ∘ f) (terminate C))
  (equiv-compose f (terminate D) e h)

Proof

Proof. This is immediate from Axiom B.4’. □

Axiom B.5 (Coproduct of categories). The coproduct of categories \(C\) and \(D\) is a category \(C\sqcup D\) equipped with inclusion functors \(i_C\colon C\to C\sqcup D\) and \(i_D\colon D\to C\sqcup D\), such that for every category \(T\) the restriction functor \[ (i_C^*,i_D^*)\colon \Map (C\sqcup D,T)\longrightarrow \Map (C,T)\times \Map (D,T) \] is an equivalence. We also call \(C\sqcup D\) the disjoint union of \(C\) and \(D\).

Agda The coproduct category

Construction 1.5.2 (Copairing). For \(f\colon C\to T\) and \(g\colon D\to T\), applying an inverse to the displayed equivalence \((i_C^*,i_D^*)\) to the pair \((f,g)\) provides a functor \[ \lra {f,g}\colon C \sqcup D \to T \] with identifications \(\lra {f,g}i_C= f\) and \(\lra {f,g}i_D= g\). For any \(h,k:C\sqcup D\to T\), restriction also induces an equivalence \[ (h= k)\iso (hi_C= ki_C)\times (hi_D= ki_D). \] To see this, use Lemma 1.3.10 for the equivalence in the coproduct axiom, then the product rule and the comparison of Construction 1.4.1. In particular, a pair of identifications \(\alpha : hi_C = ki_C\) and \(\beta : hi_D = ki_D\) results in an identification \(\lra {\alpha ,\beta }:h= k\), with the prescribed restrictions to \(C\) and \(D\).

Agda Copairing the representing points

copairPoint

Definition, checked

copairPoint : {C D E : CAT} → MAP C E → MAP D E → Obj-abs (Map (C ⊔ D) E)
Proof / implementation
copairPoint {C} {D} {E} f g =
  FunctorLift.lift (equiv-lift (coproductRestriction-isEquiv C D E) (pair (nameMap f) (nameMap g)))

copair-β₁

Derivation, checked

copair-β₁ : {C D E : CAT} (f : MAP C E) (g : MAP D E)
  → (copair f g ∘ in₁) =₁ f

  ((project-pair₁ (mapPre in₁) (mapPre in₂) (copairPoint f g)) ⁻¹ ∙

  (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G) leftSquare rightSquare

Construction 1.5.4. The formation of coproducts of categories is functorial: given two functors \(f\colon C \to C'\) and \(g\colon D \to D'\), we obtain a new functor \[ f \sqcup g := \lra {i_{C'} \circ f, i_{D'} \circ g} \colon C \sqcup D \to C' \sqcup D'. \] We leave it to the reader to verify that there are identifications \begin {align*} \id _{C} \sqcup \id _{D} = \id _{C \sqcup D} &\quadtext { and } (f' \sqcup g') \circ (f \sqcup g) = (f' \circ f) \sqcup (g' \circ g). \end {align*}

coproductMap-comp

Derivation, checked

coproductMap-comp : {C C′ C″ D D′ D″ : CAT}
  (f : MAP C C′) (f′ : MAP C′ C″) (g : MAP D D′) (g′ : MAP D′ D″)
  → (coproductMap f′ g′ ∘ coproductMap f g) =₁ (coproductMap (f′ ∘ f) (g′ ∘ g))
Proof / implementation
coproductMap-comp f f′ g g′ =
  copair-cong (comp-assoc f f′ in₁ ∙ copair-pre₁ (in₁ ∘ f′) (in₂ ∘ g′) f)
    (comp-assoc g g′ in₂ ∙ copair-pre₂ (in₁ ∘ f′) (in₂ ∘ g′) g) ∙
  copair-post (in₁ ∘ f) (in₂ ∘ g) (coproductMap f′ g′)
